# Draft:Donkey King (TV series)

----
Donkey King is an American television docuseries that premiered on 01 03 2026 on ABC stations nationwide as part of the Weekend Adventure educational and informational programming block. The series follows Ron King and the staff and volunteers at Oscar’s Place Adoption Center and Sanctuary, a nonprofit donkey rescue located in Mendocino County California. The program documents the rescue rehabilitation and rehoming of donkeys while educating viewers about donkey behavior and welfare.
Premise
Donkey King centers on the daily operations of Oscar’s Place Adoption Center and Sanctuary, a seventy five acre rescue facility in Hopland California. Each episode highlights individual donkeys with unique medical behavioral and emotional needs while showcasing the work required to prepare them for adoption. The series emphasizes compassion education and the strong bonds formed between the animals and their caretakers.
The series stars Ron King, a former media executive who left his corporate career to found Oscar’s Place. Through the show King and his team aim to change public perception of donkeys and promote humane treatment and adoption.
Production
Donkey King is produced by Hearst Media Production Group in partnership with Monument. Filming takes place on location at Oscar’s Place Adoption Center and Sanctuary in Mendocino County California.
The first season consists of seventeen episodes.
Broadcast
The series premiered on ABC on 01 03 2026 and airs on weekend mornings as part of the Weekend Adventure block.
Cast
* Ron King founder and director of Oscar’s Place Adoption Center and Sanctuary
Setting
Donkey King is set primarily at Oscar’s Place Adoption Center and Sanctuary in Hopland Mendocino County California. The nonprofit organization focuses on rescuing rehabilitating and rehoming donkeys that would otherwise face neglect abandonment or slaughter.
Reception
Early media coverage has described Donkey King as heartwarming and educational. Good Housekeeping praised the series for highlighting the emotional intelligence of donkeys and the dedication of the rescue staff.
People Magazine noted that the show brings attention to an often overlooked animal while telling uplifting stories centered on rescue compassion and second chances.
